mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% over three months signals weakening consumer demand and earnings pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three months signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of three-month RSAFS decline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production over three months signals weakening manufacturing activity and profit pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of three-month INDPRO decline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in CPI above 2.5% over six months signals persistent inflation, prompting tighter monetary policy and higher discount rates, which reduces S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of sustained CPI > 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05).
